liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Cryptical Envelopment** (4 reviews): Reviewer notes this was the first Cryptical Envelopment in 13 years; Cryptical Envelopment frames The Other One, returning after it in a Cryptical, Other One, Cryptical sequence [31][32][33][35]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Jerry's solo in Bertha is barely audible on the soundboard [38]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Phil's bass bomb that begins The Other One is praised as sounding almost computer-made [32]
- **space** (1 review): Space is full of birdlike chirps and buzzing insects, called a hilarious mind-bender at Weir's expense [40]

## Setlist highlights

- **Cryptical Envelopment**: back after 866 archived shows (4649 days) [41]

## The recordings

- **gd85-06-16.sbd.braveman.26080.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 149 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [1]. Said about its sound: Soundboard is described as good quality with a good balance [35]
- **gd85-06-16.oade.sacks.7087.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 153 min; rated 4.36/5 by 22 [2]. Said about its sound: Audience tape has a decent mix emphasizing vocals and leads, with clear sound but somewhat lacking bass [39]
- **gd85-06-16.sbd.barrick.970.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 141 min; rated 3.83/5 by 6 [5]. Said about its sound: Vocals and bass are very prominent on most tracks, while Jerry's guitar sounds washed out and nearly inaudible; No crowd noise at all, giving a studio-like feel; Resolution is high with a studio-like sound; crowd noise appears only between songs, not during them [29][30][38]
- **gd1985-06-16.167183.neumann.km84i.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 144 min [8]
- **gd1985-06-16.senn441.mccue.ford.33669.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 118 min [10]. Said about its sound: A dying battery in the D5 recorder is audible; Midnight Hour has static and a mic adjustment, and some tape is garbled [10]
- **gd1985-06-16.152521.sbd.fixed.cm.miller.t.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 151 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [11]

## Around the show

- Attendee says it marked the 20th anniversary of Phil moving to where the band lived [33]
- A Sunday afternoon show in beautiful weather starting at 5:00; Saturday began at 7 and Friday at 9 [33]
- Last night of a three-night run, commonly called the 20th anniversary shows [35]
- Reviewer's cousin attended and said it was the furthest he ever swam from shore [40]
- Reviewer does not fully recommend this soundboard over the Oade audience recording [29]
- Reviewer says fans of fast-paced 1985 shows will like this one [38]
- Reviewer misses Phil's booming bass bombs heard in bigger halls [39]
- Reviewer finds this space far better than the long, tedious spaces of the 1990s [40]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd85-06-16.sbd.braveman.26080.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by jbraveman; source: SBD > Reel Master > DATs [1]. Also: Soundboard to Reel Master to DATs, transferred by jbraveman, who used a 60ES DAT deck and a USB audio interface; Transfer was normalized and given minor edits in Goldwave, then encoded with mkwACT [1]
- **gd85-06-16.oade.sacks.7087.sbeok.shnf**: source: Oade PCM-AUD -- Schoeps MK41 (90 deg ORTF -- Tapers' Section) -> CMC4 ->Oade M118 prototype [2]. Also: Reviewer's old car-deck tape of the show was said by its giver to be stolen from a band member [37]
- **gd85-06-16.sbd.barrick.970.sbefail.shnf**: source: source update: SBD> MVHS> DAT> CD-R [5]. Also: Reviewer has owned a second-generation soundboard tape since 1988; this SHN version sounds very close to it [30]
- **gd1985-06-16.167183.neumann.km84i.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Chris Hecht; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Chris Hecht's Master Audience Cassettes; Neumann KM84i mics > Sony D5M [8]. Also: Master recording came from Chris Hecht; Charlie Miller handled the transfer. Filename lists Neumann KM84i microphones; A Nakamichi 700 source from Mark Severson patches a 0:09 gap in the Looks Like Rain to Half-Step transition and 1:51 in Drums [8]
- **gd1985-06-16.senn441.mccue.ford.33669.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Adam, Justin & Monica; transferred by Alex Ford; source: (FOB) 2 Sennheiser 441's > Sony D5 > Master Cassettes [10]. Also: Fileset omits the last three tracks of disc two: Wharf Rat, Lovelight and Brokedown Palace [10]
- **gd1985-06-16.152521.sbd.fixed.cm.miller.t.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  April 22, 2021; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550/Maxell XLII-S90) [11]. Also: Sourced from tapes from Joani Walker and Paul Scotton, with a PCM soundboard covering tape flips; pitch-corrected, 24-bit [11]

A dying battery in the D5 recorder is audible; Midnight Hour has static and a mic adjustment, and some tape is garbled
Fileset omits the last three tracks of disc two: Wharf Rat, Lovelight and Brokedown Palace
Sourced from tapes from Joani Walker and Paul Scotton, with a PCM soundboard covering tape flips; pitch-corrected, 24-bit

Reviewer does not fully recommend this soundboard over the Oade audience recording

The mix shifts as the show goes on, with Jerry sometimes deeper in the mix
Reviewer notes this was the first Cryptical Envelopment in 13 years

Cryptical Envelopment frames The Other One, returning after it in a Cryptical, Other One, Cryptical sequence
Attendee says it marked the 20th anniversary of Phil moving to where the band lived
A Sunday afternoon show in beautiful weather starting at 5:00; Saturday began at 7 and Friday at 9
Reviewer thinks the full Cryptical Envelopment had not been played in over ten years

Soundboard is described as good quality with a good balance

Reviewer says fans of fast-paced 1985 shows will like this one

Reviewer misses Phil's booming bass bombs heard in bigger halls
